workItem.title: Bridge-readiness: MIT runtime settings CLI terminal entrypoint IAU candidate

targetGap.summary: The MIT authority has pure command, settings, validation, proof, and interactive-selection contracts, but it has no public import, Spec Kit feature, admission record, or clean-room contract for the materialized bare vihs terminal entrypoint and its runtime recovery facts.

splitDecision.reason: Terminal entrypoint materialization should establish the public command-surface and recovery facts before the MIT authority binds those facts to process-level stdin/TTY prompt behavior.
doNotAdmitTogether: raw terminal prompt loops and stdin/TTY handling
proof-out file writing beyond already admitted proof artifact contracts
live already-running VS Code session uptake proof

allowed: requirement IDs VHS-REQ-537, VHS-REQ-544, VHS-REQ-545, and VHS-REQ-546
supporting public test expectations for terminal entrypoint materialization, runtime recovery, no-argument discoverability, and validation handoff
package identity vi-history / VI History / svelderrainruiz / MIT / 0.1.0
user-scope terminal entrypoint admission facts for supported installed-user shells
rules that no hidden path reconstruction, manual shell-profile editing, admin elevation, machine-wide install doctrine, or prebuilt external CLI payload is required
runtime lookup order facts, including standard VS Code runtime on Windows before global Node fallback or explicit override
stale or missing launcher recovery guidance through the governed repair or refresh path
no-argument discoverability fields that may print the current provider/platform/LabVIEW version/LabVIEW bitness bundle and exact copyable next commands
validation handoff semantics for a later prompt-loop IAU, reusing the existing public vihs --validate contract
blocked: private evidence roots or local filesystem paths
credentials, token names, or release credentials
source-copying instructions from another VI History authority
GitLab implementation source or private proof packets
raw prompt-loop stdin handling before a later IAU
live already-running VS Code session uptake proof
VSIX packaging, Marketplace publication, or release automation

candidateImplementationWork: add tests proving a materialized vihs terminal entrypoint is represented without requiring hidden-path reconstruction, profile editing, admin elevation, machine-wide install doctrine, or a prebuilt external CLI payload
add tests proving supported terminal-session admission records stay user-scoped and expose the intended entrypoint state
add tests proving runtime lookup and recovery facts prefer the standard VS Code runtime on Windows before global Node fallback or explicit override
add tests proving stale or missing launchers fail closed with one stable actionable recovery instruction
implement the minimum public MIT materialized-entrypoint contract as pure command-surface facts and command plans, without invoking a runtime process

candidateTasks: add tests for materialized vihs terminal entrypoint facts
add tests for user-scope terminal-session admission state
add tests for runtime lookup order and override facts
add tests for stale or missing launcher fail-closed recovery guidance
implement a pure materialized-entrypoint command-surface contract
blockedTasks: raw terminal prompt loops and stdin/TTY handling
no-argument confirmation flow beyond already implemented pure selection-state facts
proof-out file writing beyond already admitted proof artifact contracts
live already-running VS Code session uptake proof
source copying from GitLab or GitHub Suite

candidateTasks: bind the pure interactive-selection contract to process-level no-argument vihs prompt behavior
add Enter-through confirmation and guided selection prompt-loop tests
add validation handoff tests after prompt-loop confirmation

allowedNextWork: create the public MIT import packet for runtime-settings-cli-terminal-entrypoint-v1
create the public Spec Kit feature spec, plan, and tasks
add public admission records with implementationStartAllowed false until preflight passes
run public redaction and artifact validation
